study_identification_part.si_4_title: Lifespan Normative Modeling of Brain Microstructure

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression normative model estimated with HBR (PCNtoolkit) for DTI metrics across sites.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We extracted regional diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics using a standardized analysis and quality control protocol and used hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) to model the statistical distribution of derived WM metrics as a function of age and sex.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: DTI metrics (FA, MD, AD, RD) extracted from 21 deep WM regions plus Global-WM.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: We fitted normative models to four diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics (FA, MD, AD, RD) from 21 deep WM regions and the 'Global-WM' (a single metric including the entire WM)
nm2_2_response_variable.location: VillalonReina2024.pdf.md: Results / 2.1. Lifespan trajectories of brain microstructural metrics

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age modeled as a fixed independent variable; sex as a grouping variable; dMRI protocol used as the batch effect in HBR.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text:
used hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) to model the statistical distribution of derived WM metrics as a function of age and sex.
Consequently, we used the dMRI protocol as the batch effect when training the normative model with HBR... included sex as a second grouping variable in the HBR setting, and age as a fixed independent variable.
